questions.title: Terminal velocity of a paper cone
questions.summary: Time a filter-paper cone falling at terminal velocity, then cut a smaller cone and test v ∝ 1/d. Plan a loaded-cone (paperclip) experiment and find the energy dissipated from the area under a drag force–distance graph.

xlsx.desc: A practice version of datasetQ1h: drag force F against distance s. Area under the graph (trapezium rule) up to 1.000 m.

questions.title: Five-resistor network
questions.summary: Moving the tapping X brings the fifth resistor in parallel with n of the chain. 1/I = −(R/E)·n²/(n+1) + 4R/E: plot 1/I against n²/(n+1), then R = −gradient × E.

xlsx.desc: Five (n, I) readings. Plot 1/I against n²/(n+1).

questions.title: Bifilar suspension (playground ride model)
questions.summary: A half-metre rule hangs from two string loops a distance d apart and twists about a vertical axis. Test T² = kl/d² with two set-ups, then plan and carry out a study of how two masses at ±x change T: T² is linear in x², and the intercept C gives I₀.

xlsx.desc: Six positions x with two timings each. Plot T² against x² and find C.

notes.text: Key idea: the loaded cone falls faster, so it needs a longer drop to reach terminal velocity and electronic timing (light gates or video) instead of a stopwatch.
The force rises towards the weight 0.020 N as the cone approaches terminal velocity, so the area is less than W × 1.000 m = 0.020 J.

Compare with y = mx + c: y = 1/I, x = n²/(n + 1), gradient −R/E, y-intercept 4R/E.
